whatAre.title: What is GBSV?
whatAre.content: Gender-Based and Sexual Violence encompasses all forms of physical, psychological or sexual violence exercised on the basis of sex, gender identity or sexual orientation.

types.title: Types of violence
types.content: Harassment, physical or sexual assault, rape, domestic violence, cyberbullying, discrimination... Every form of violence is serious and unacceptable.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.content: You have the right to be protected, helped and supported. No one has the right to harm your physical or psychological integrity.

intervention.title: How to intervene safely
intervention.subtitle: Learn safe intervention techniques, the steps to follow and secret codes to help victims of GBSV.

method3d.title: The 3D Method - How to intervene safely
method3d.intro: These techniques aim to act without putting your own safety at risk:

delegate.label: DELEGATE
delegate.description: Alert a manager, contact security or emergency services

distract.label: DISTRACT
distract.description: Interrupt the scene with an innocent question or distraction

dialogue.label: DIALOGUE
dialogue.description: If the situation allows, speak directly to the aggressor or the victim

whatToDo.title: What to do step by step?

steps.title: Ensure immediate safety
steps.description: If you sense a victim is in danger, intervene without putting yourself at risk or create a diversion (ask the time, approach as if you know them). Otherwise, call 17 or send an SMS to 114.

steps.title: Support the victim
steps.description: Stay with the victim, ask if they are okay and listen without judgment. Do not minimize what they have just experienced. Reassure them that they are not alone.

steps.title: Do not confront the aggressor
steps.description: You don't have to play the hero. Protect the victim and gather useful information (location, description, time) to alert the authorities.

steps.title: Offer concrete help
steps.description: Accompany the victim to file a complaint, see a doctor or call 3919 or 17. Offer to testify if you saw or heard what happened.

steps.title: Report the facts
steps.description: In transport: alert button, SNCF/RATP agents, 'STOP Harassment' app. At university/work: management or equality officer. Online: Pharos (internet-signalement.gouv.fr).

angelShot.title: Angel Shot – What is it?
angelShot.subtitle: The "Angel Shot" is a discreet code used mainly in bars and nightclubs. It allows a person to signal to the staff that they are in danger or uncomfortable, without alerting the potential aggressor.

neat.label: "Angel shot neat"
neat.description: Request to be walked to their car

ice.label: "Angel shot with ice"
ice.description: Request to call a taxi or Uber

angela.title: Ask for "Angela"
angela.description: A system originally set up in the United Kingdom ("Ask for Angela") to protect against street harassment.
angela.content: If you feel in danger or are being harassed in the street, ask this question in a shop, restaurant or cultural venue (identifiable by a purple badge). This triggers a help procedure.

apps.title: Emergency apps
apps.content: Some apps allow you to alert a trusted contact, call emergency services or share your location. On Android you can press the power button five times quickly to automatically trigger an emergency call. The Emergency app on iPhone allows you to quickly call emergency services and automatically share your vital medical information when needed.

hand.title: The distress hand signal
hand.content: An internationally recognized gesture to discreetly alert others:
steps: Fold the thumb into the palm
hand.saved: This signal has already saved several victims!

cta.title: Acting safely saves lives
cta.content: Every intervention can make a difference. Do not hesitate to use these techniques and share this information around you.

resources.title: Resources and help
resources.subtitle: Find here all the resources to help you or help someone who is a victim of gender-based and sexual violence.

harassment.label: Sexual harassment
harassment.definition: Repeated conduct or behavior of a sexual nature that undermines dignity (art. 222-33 of the French Penal Code)
harassment.penalty: 2 years imprisonment and €30,000 fine (aggravated: 3 years and €45,000)

assault.label: Sexual assault
assault.definition: Sexual act committed with violence, coercion, threat or surprise (art. 222-22 of the French Penal Code)
assault.penalty: 5 years imprisonment and €75,000 fine (aggravated: 7 years and €100,000)

rape.label: Rape
rape.definition: Act of sexual penetration committed with violence, coercion, threat or surprise (art. 222-23 of the French Penal Code)

about.p1: Erinyes is a awareness website dedicated to fighting against gender-based and sexual violence (GBSV). Our mission is to break the silence, inform and support victims towards appropriate help resources.
about.p2: In Greek mythology, the Erinyes were the goddesses of vengeance who pursued criminals and ensured justice was served. Today, we carry this symbolic name to defend victims and fight against impunity.
about.quote: "Let's stop normalizing domination and sexualization, and instead normalize the consent of others. Listen, understand and respect the desires and needs of each person. When it's no, it's NO!"
about.p3: Our platform offers updated statistics, help resources, awareness training and prevention tools to contribute to a world free from gender-based and sexual violence.
